Acro Aircraft Seating designs and manufactures economy airline seats for the low-cost carrier market. Its range includes both fixed and reclining seats, as well as premium economy seats.
During BGF’s investment, the business increased sales by around 20%, launched two new series of economy seats and won a contract with Airbus, extending its reach to newly built aircraft. Acro received the Queen’s Award for International Trade in 2015.
In 2017, Acro was acquired by Zhejiang Science and Technology Investment Company to help to accelerate Acro’s access to the Chinese market.

Unlocking a smarter way to recycle e-waste
Electronic waste (e-waste) is one of the world’s fastest-growing economic and environmental challenges. But DEScycle’s 
novel approach to metal recycling technology
 has the potential to deliver a clean, scalable solution to this challenge, at a critical time. We’re excited to be backing the business, as it looks to bring this much-needed innovation to the industrial level.
E-waste is surging
In 2022, the world generated 
~62 million tonnes of e-waste
, equating to 7-8kg for every person on the planet — an increase of more than 80% since 2010. That number could hit 82 million tonnes by 2030.

Disrupting an industry long dominated by diesel incumbents, Sunswap’s electric TRU alternative is cheaper to run, easier to maintain, and smarter to operate.

Its technology enables donor livers to be maintained in a functioning state, outside the human body, for up to 24 hours — significantly increasing the number of viable organs available for transplant and improving patient outcomes.
We first invested in OrganOx in 2019, and participated in seven rounds of investment, becoming the company’s largest shareholder. Our investment and support, along with that of an incredible group of co-investors and independent board members, helped the business scale into a world-leading medtech.

Reeve the Baker
Legendary Bakers: our new investment in Reeve the Baker
We are delighted to announce our investment in 
Reeve the Baker
, the much-loved, third-generation regional bakery renowned for its high-quality bread and baked goods, baked fresh every day.
We are partnering with Gary Reeve and Managing Director Mathieu Le Bras, previously MD of Gail’s The Bread Factory. They are joined by new Chairman Nick Collins, CEO of our former partner brand Loungers, which has grown to over 300 sites nationwide. Our investment will help Reeve grow across the market towns of the South of England, reaching communities who have been asking for a Reeve of their own for many years.
We have a long track record of backing food and drink brands from the South-West with their own manufacturing, including Devon-based premium dog food brand Forthglade and Gloucestershire-based drinks brand Bottlegreen.
Loved for generations
Harold Reeve founded the family business in 1952. His son Ray opened the first shop in Wilton in 1971. Three generations on, with Gary Reeve at the helm, Reeve has grown to 13 shops across Wiltshire and Hampshire, with a new Dorchester shop opening in November.
Reeve employs over 200 people and turns over £12m, making it a significant local employer. The brand runs deep in family histories, and we have met many people in the area who remember working there with real fondness.
There is so much history to lean on. Early on, we were handed one of only three copies of 
Memories of a Village Baker
, Ray Reeve’s own history of the business. It felt like being handed a first folio, and a sign of how much the heritage and family values matter. Inside is a photo of Harold’s 1934 recipe book and a whole section on the right way to fry doughnuts.
For Gary, protecting his family’s legacy was at the heart of the decision to partner with us: “For more than seven decades, Reeve the Baker has been part of the daily lives of our customers and communities. Finding the right partner to help secure the future of the business was incredibly important to us. Piper shares our belief in the strength of the Reeve brand, our people and our values. This investment gives us the opportunity to continue growing while staying true to everything that has made Reeve the Baker special.”

Vieve
We are delighted to announce our investment in 
VIEVE
, the fast-growing cosmetics brand built by renowned Scottish makeup artist Jamie Genevieve.
This marks Piper’s latest commitment to backing exceptional brands across beauty, wellness and lifestyle. We are thrilled to partner with a brand dedicated to empowering real people through high-quality, innovative make-up. Piper has invested £65m in female-led brands in the last two funds, including two thirds of the latest fund’s investments.
Founded in 2020, VIEVE has rapidly established itself as a force in the beauty industry that champions creativity and self-expression, with a loyal following and a reputation for high-quality, skin-loving formulas. The brand is at the forefront of the growing “skinification” of make-up, with 83% of women looking for added skincare benefits in their make-up. This shift has accelerated the success of VIEVE’s award winning bestseller, Skin Nova, a hybrid formula that bridges the gap between skincare and make-up.
Jamie’s Scottish heritage is at the heart of the brand, where her authenticity and creativity have inspired a loyal community. Jamie honed her craft on make-up counters in Glasgow, working closely with customers to understand their needs and fill them with confidence. Her artistry expertise and relatable approach to beauty later found a wider audience through YouTube, where she built an international following of over 2 million across Instagram and YouTube.
Born from a passionate beauty community, VIEVE has excelled as a brand embraced by professional make-up artists, who champion its performance-driven formulas, and everyday users alike. The brand is loved by its customers with an NPS of 84 and a product satisfaction score of 9.5/10. VIEVE’s high-quality, easy-to-use and non-intimidating products, combined with accessible “how-to” tutorials, empowers people to enjoy make-up as part of their wellbeing routine.
Since launching in 2020, VIEVE has achieved impressive growth, with revenue rising from £6.5m in 2024 to a forecasted £10m in 2025. The brand has a well-balanced approach to both D2C and retail channels, including their own experiential store in Glasgow, where customers can attend exclusive masterclasses with Jamie, and discover can’t-get-them-anywhere-else products and special residencies from local businesses. We’re delighted to announce our £7.5 million investment in Borough Broth, the British organic bone broth brand on a mission to make sustainable, nutrient-rich food mainstream. A brand born from purpose
Founded in 2015 by Ros Heathcote with just £6,000 borrowed from a friend, Borough Broth began life in a small London kitchen. During a personal health crisis, Ros rediscovered the healing power of bone broth chicken soup from her childhood. Frustrated by the lack of high-quality options, she started selling her slow-cooked, organic broths at local markets and online, pioneering the UK broth category. With no prior experience in the food industry, Ros transitioned from a career in data analysis and business intelligence to create a business built on precision, integrity and purpose.
Ten years on, Borough Broth has grown into one of the UK’s fastest-growing organic, B Corp–certified and female founded brands. Today it has revenues of more than £10 million, growing +93% year-on-year, and is stocked in Waitrose, Sainsbury’s, Tesco, Ocado and independents across the UK. Its award-winning range – from classic chicken and beef broths to Tonkotsu Ramen and Pho – has earned 14 Great Taste Awards and multiple BOOM (Best of Organic Market) wins.
Why Borough Broth?
Borough Broth sits at the intersection of taste, health, sustainability and convenience, tapping into consumer demand while driving behaviour change with its versatility:
• 57% of customers primarily use it as a cooking ingredient to add depth to soups, sauces, stews and roasts.
• 24% drink it as a hot, comforting beverage.
• 19% consume it for functional benefits like gut health and immune support.
High in protein and collagen, they’re also popular for longevity and increasingly feature in GLP-1 diets thanks to their low-carb, high-protein profile. While most enjoy them at lunch or dinner, one in five customers start their day with a broth as a health boost or to break a fast.

Being on the brink of burnout was the catalyst for Nicola Elliott to make a radical change. As a national magazine journalist, she regularly worked 60-hour weeks, flying around the world interviewing celebrities – a glamorous but frenetic existence. So Elliott quit journalism to train as an aromatherapist and nutritionist and soon began creating her own aromatherapy blends. First was ‘Tranquillity’ for her sister who was having trouble sleeping. Then came ‘Real Luxury’ to help her own anxiety and stress, followed by ‘Feel Refreshed’ for her husband who played lots of sport and needed an energy boost.

Products are designed to help with four key need states: stress, sleep, happiness and energy, working either on your personal environment through candles and diffusers, or on your skin and body through skincare and bath & body products.  All products are made in Britain from ethically sourced, sustainable origins, using only natural and organic ingredients, no petrochemical paraffin or mineral waxes, no artificial perfumes, only pure essential oils and no harsh preservatives.
Our own research into the wellness market had highlighted that consumers were increasingly concerned about their wellbeing, and having discovered NEOM soon after it was established in 2008, we were attracted to the brand that could help customers make it easy for them to feel their best every day. Bloom & Wild
Building the leading European online flower gifting brand legend that enhances the joy of sending and receiving flowers.
Invested £15m in 2018
When looking at new brands, the first question we always ask ourselves is: ‘Is it better and different than the competition?’. With Bloom & Wild, the answer was an emphatic ‘yes!’. Founded in 2013 by Aron Gelbard and Ben Stanway, it has single-handedly disrupted and revolutionised Europe’s £14bn fresh cut flower market.
The story of commercial flower delivery goes back more than a century – and, until 
Bloom & Wild
 arrived on the scene, the concept essentially remained the same. Flowers would be delivered to your home. If you weren’t in to receive them, you would return home to a note and have to pick them up from a neighbour or local florist. These flowers normally came direct from local florists but were often not the specific bouquets ordered but ‘similar’ types, and far from being fresh, had been in transit and in the florists for a number of days.
Bloom & Wild took this model and turned it on its head. In an age where our lives are busier than ever, it made no sense to waste time having to hunt down a gift. Receiving flowers should be a pleasure not a chore. And, as for the flowers themselves, why couldn’t they be exactly the same as those ordered, and shipped direct from the grower?
So Aron and Ben pioneered the award-winning concept of ‘letterbox flowers’ – allowing customers the ability to gift fresh flowers in a convenient slim box that fits through the receiver’s letterbox. This initially involved Aron walking around London with a notebook and ruler, measuring thousands of letterboxes and typing them all up into a spread sheet. He used this to calculate how small a box would need to be to get through about 90 per cent of letterboxes.
The founders also invested heavily in technology to transform both the customer experience and the traditional supply chain. Bloom & Wild flowers do not come from local florists but direct from the producers themselves – giving customers beautiful, high quality fresh flowers. The flowers are delivered in bud, protected by a special casing, so they bloom over time and last longer than other bouquets.
The results speak for themselves. Revenues hit £10m within three years of launch and more than 50 million Bloom & Wild flowers have been shipped to date across the UK, Fr

Owners can drop their dogs off or they can be collected by one of Bruce’s 18 specially adapted and air-conditioned doggy buses. Building a disruptive steak restaurant brand legend that challenges stuffy and over-priced steakhouses by serving the best quality steaks at great prices off a famously simple menu in a casual environment.

How do you launch a business in a crowded and competitive market? By being a cut above the rest.
In Charlie Carroll’s case, the cut was literal. Working in the restaurant industry, he had noticed that the steak market was served either by good quality but very expensive high-end establishments or by poor quality, mass market offers.
Flat Iron
 was created to challenge traditional perceptions of steak, offering customers a modern take on the traditional steak house – no fuss, no frills, just delicious,high quality steak for £10. How was it achievable at this price point? By being smart and innovative. Instead of opting for the more familiar, expensive cuts – such as fillet, sirloin and rib-eye – Carroll identified the secondary cut known as the ‘flat iron’ and taken from the shoulder blade. This not only gave his restaurant its USP – and name – but also gave it buying power with suppliers and unrivalled expertise in this area of the market.
The first Flat Iron opened in 2012 as a pop up above the Owl & Pussycat pub in Shoreditch, London. It proved such a success that a permanent site was opened later that year in Beak Street in Soho. Its second restaurant opened in Denmark Street in 2014, with a ceremonial spit roasting of a whole ox. Long queues became a regular feature outside its third site in Covent Garden, which boasted its own working butcher’s shop.
The company also owns a herd of cattle on its farm in North Yorkshire and is rightly proud of its beef – so much so that its chalkboards highlight the cows’ breed, where they were born and even their finishing diet. Such care and attention to detail are all part of the Flat Iron experience and have helped the group to build a loyal and evangelical band of customers.
Having heard about the legendary queues outside Flat Iron restaurants we built a relationship with Charlie that led to a £10m investment into Flat Iron in 2017, to provide the company with the necessary funding to help him build the team, focus on delivering outstanding quality, continue to develop a beacon brand of excellence and open further units in and around London.

Frame
The feel-good disruptive fitness brand with a highly engaged community of Framers seeking fun fitness classes.
Invested £6M in 2017. Exited in 2022
While the UK’s £5bn fitness industry today offers a dizzying wealth of choice, back in 2008 the fitness experience was an entirely different proposition. Cardio consisted of pounding a treadmill. Weights rooms were out of bounds for non-Olympians. Membership was purposely inflexible, tying gym-goers into 12-month minimum length contracts.
The model was out of shape and badly in need of an energy boost. Enter the boutique fitness brand Frame. Friends and former competitive athletes Pip Black and Joan Murphy had searched in vain for a gym or fitness studio in London that would give them the flexibility, variety, and fun they wanted. Realising it didn’t exist, they decided to create one themselves. The first Frame studio opened in Shoreditch in 2009.
Variety is central to the Frame proposition, born from Pip and Joan’s belief that it helps keep customers’ fitness routines fresh, engaging and better for the body. Classes include everything from the unforgettable ‘Kylie Butt Lift’ and ‘Bend It Like Barbie’ to the more meditative ‘Detox Yoga.’
As well as ripping up the rulebook on types of exercise, Frame was also an early pioneer in changing the way the sessions are provided. Out went the old membership model, in came the ‘drop in’ and pay-as-you-go Frame Card system, with bookings taken on a user-friendly mobile system.
Recognising that Frame had created an innovative, industry leading boutique fitness model, we invested £6m into Frame in 2017 to help the brand expand. At the time of investment there were four Frame sites in London (Shoreditch, King’s Cross, Victoria, and Queen’s Park) with further sites opening in Hammersmith, Angel, and Soho.
We have developed a close partnership with Piper and are already seeing the benefits of working with their wider team, drawing on their skills and experience.
Pip Black, Co-founder

Even the greatest music artists have succumbed to the difficult second album syndrome. For entrepreneurs, the challenges of launching and succeeding with a second business are considerably more pronounced. Place that business in the restaurant and hospitality sector and the odds against them are stacked even higher.
Which makes the story of 
Turtle Bay
 all the more remarkable. Ajith Jaya-Wickrema moved from Sri Lanka to the UK at the age of 15, speaking no English. He learned it from watching Newsnight and reading editorials of The Times newspaper and later gained a place at Birmingham University to study economics. Having been laid off by a management consultancy early in his career, he pretended to his bank manager that he wanted to buy a car – and instead used the £10,000 loan to open his first restaurant, the Latin American-themed Las Iguanas, in Bristol.
He and his co-founder grew the chain to four sites – the point at which we invested in the business. Our aim was to help them develop sites in prime locations and build a management team around them to support such growth. During this period, the estate grew to 16 sites and became the UK’s market leading Latin American chain. In 2007, we successfully exited Las Iguanas, delivering a 6x multiple on our investment.
Many founders might have chosen to leave it there. But in 2010, Ajith, having left Las Iguanas, turned his attention to another style of cuisine: Caribbean. He decided to create a group of restaurants which would ‘transport you to the Caribbean without a plane ticket’ – and Turtle Bay was born.
The first site opened in Milton Keynes – perhaps not the most obvious choice of location. To paraphrase Frank Sinatra: if you can make it there, you can make it anywhere. And, indeed, Turtle Bay did just that – it took off immediately.
Turtle Bay’s success is based on providing a uniquely Caribbean experience, with a centralised island bar serving rum-based cocktails both day and night, a menu that combines Caribbean spices with fragrant marinades, hot sauces, cooling chutneys and fresh fruit, with its signature jerk chicken grill at the heart of the rest

Boden
The stylishly casual clothing catalogue business that went online and became an early international direct-to-consumer success story.
Invested in 1999, and exited in 2007
When Johnnie Boden launched the business in 1991 his focus was on clothing for men. By 1999, when Piper came to invest, Boden was not just designing clothing not just men, but women and children too. Their turnover had grown to £18m and the brand was competing directly with the likes of M&S and Gap.
Although growth had been rapid, founder Johnnie and MD Julian Granville recognised the business faced challenges. Capital was needed to grow the business, but it was needed alongside partner support that went beyond money. Our partnership began as the brand was launching its online store, and with our expertise and focused experience, they were able to avoid the distraction of becoming a retailer and instead grow a highly efficient and effective direct-to-consumer brand.
During our involvement, we helped the business build a clear and confident brand positioning. In addition, Piper worked closely with management to define the shape of the organisation. Boden became one of the UK’s most well-known brands and we supported their international expansion into Europe and the USA.
In 2007 we sold our stake, achieving a 30x multiple. With sales growing from £20m to over £150m and US sales delivering over $100m. Despite exiting, the Piper non-executives were asked to remain on the Board. “We really rate them. The fact that I’ve asked them to stay on the Board, even though they are selling – that says it all” stated Johnnie Boden.
We really rate Piper. The fact that we asked them to stay on the Board, even though they were no longer investors – that says it all

Maximuscle
The sports nutrition brand created by experts that disrupted the market with its focus on protein, fitness and results.
Invested in 2004, exited 2007
Maximuscle was founded in 1995 by Zef Eisenberg. Following a career as a highly successful bodybuilder, he published an exposé of the industry’s marketing hype based on his research into which products would work to build muscle and burn fat. On the back of a sell-out print run of his book, Zef started to offer specific products he trusted through a small mail order catalogue, which eventually grew into a brand selling its own products.
In 2002 Zef won the Young Entrepreneur of the Year Award. By 2004 turnover at Maximuscle was £8m, but growth had stalled. This prompted the decision to bring in a partner and help the business with the next stage of growth. As an expert in growth and taking businesses out of the entrepreneurial stage, Piper enabled its founder to realise some value from the business and to use additional funding to develop a professional management team and build the brand.
The business was able to rapidly grow using our experience of direct retailing to drive up customer recruitment and retention and using customer insight to plug into the growing trend in healthy eating, exercise and looking good. The benefits of its high protein products were being sold direct to consumers, reaching a dedicated consumer base through its online platform as well as a wider market through high street chains such as Argos, Tesco and JJB sports, gyms and specialist sports stores. This strategy led to a 3x increase in sales.
In 2007 we sold Maximuscle to Darwin Private Equity for £75m, providing Piper with a 10x multiple on its investment in just over three years. After exit, Maximuscle continued its incredible growth and into 2010 it was sold to GSK for £162M.
They add unique value through their customer understanding. They genuinely know how to grow brands

The Rug Company was founded in 1997 by husband and wife team Christopher and Suzanne Sharp, who recognised a gap in the market for artisan quality contemporary rugs. Their first store opened in Holland Park, London in 1997 and their products are handmade and produced using traditional weaving skills in Nepal.
Having successfully grown the business to 8 stores, Chris and Suzanne Sharp felt it was time to bring in a partner to help them achieve their ambitious growth plans.
In 2008, Piper invested to help them grow out of entrepreneurial phase by expanding internationally and building a professional management team to support that expansion. Piper was actively involved in helping to develop and recruit the team, introducing a Chairman, Finance Director, and Marketing Director into the business, as well as helping to structure an appropriate sales team.
The business grew its range to more than 300 rug designs, including its own Contemporary Collection developed by the company’s in-house design team, and its Designer Collection featuring collaborations with over 30 designers from the worlds of fashion, interior design, and textiles (such as Alexander McQueen, Paul Smith, and Vivienne Westwood).
Our close involvement enabled the brand to more than double sales from £11m to £23m and expand worldwide with 12 new store openings including four owned stores in USA and franchise partners in Dubai, Mexico, Canada, Hong Kong, San Francisco, Taiwan, and Lebanon.
In 2015 we sold our stake in The Rug Company to Palamon Capital Partners.

Pitcher & Piano
The fun and friendly bar chain that reinvented the way we socialise.
Founded in 1985, exited 1996
Piper’s origins are entwined with the founding of the iconic bar chain, Pitcher & Piano. We started out as a strategic consumer brand consultancy in 1985, working with top retail, FMCG, and leisure brands. When a pitch for a new bar concept got rejected, our founders Crispin and Libby saw an opportunity to create something truly different that they couldn’t let go.
Pitcher & Piano was a new kind of bar for a new generation. At a time when the market was split between stuffy wine bars and rough-and-ready pubs, we spotted a gap. A casual bar experience that catered to women as much as men, combining great drinks, friendly service, and a buzzing, piano-accompanied vibe. It heralded a new breed of bars and restaurants that challenged the status quo, disrupting the traditional pub and wine bar scenes that had dominated for decades. Our first site in Fulham drew in crowds from day one.
When coming up with the concept and envisioning the brand, Crispin sat down and wrote the aspirational philosophy that would guide Pitcher & Piano. It opens with, 
‘The aim of Pitcher & Piano is to be the best known bar in Britain. To become a legend in our own lifetime, the chain that sets the standard for the competition.’
 This framed philosophy still hangs in our office today, a proud reminder of where it all began and the origins of our expression, brand legend.
Over the next decade, we transformed standout locations like old banks and churches into vibrant social spaces. Within the bars themselves we prioritised training and supporting our staff, understanding that happy, well-supported teams deliver outstanding customer experiences.
In 1996, we sold Pitcher & Piano to Marstons plc for £20m.
Pitcher & Piano lives on today with 16 sites across the UK and a legacy of transforming how people socialise. It was our first “brand legend,” and it embodies the values that continue to drive us: building innovative and enduring brands that customers love.
Piper: Building brand legends since 1985.

The sofa retailer who became an early pioneer in the direct-to-consumer market.

Andrew Cussins founded Sofa Workshop in 1985, opening its first store in Maidstone the following year.

A subscription based wellness brand
Sector

Absolute Collagen is a direct-to-consumer, subscription based wellness brand, principally offering marine collagen supplements intended to deliver skin, hair and health benefits.
The business was founded in 2015 by Maxine Laceby, after she experienced positive skin and wellbeing benefits attributed to the collagen contained in homemade bone broths. Disappointed by the low concentration and multitude of bulking agents in collagen supplements available at the time, she set out to create a pure collagen product with the highest bioavailability and efficacy, launching ready-mixed sachets of hydrolysed marine collagen in 2017.
Since then, Absolute Collagen has grown a loyal subscriber following (or “Absoluters”), with strong consumer advocacy and endorsement from professional dermatologists and trichologists. In 2019 the business also won Best New Beauty Supplement – Mass & Prestige at the prestigious CEW Awards. Today Absolute Collagen offers marine collagen supplement in three flavours as well as a topical collagen facial serum, with further products in development.

Air Energi is an international manpower services business specialising in the oil and gas sector providing contract, project and staff hire engineers and technical specialists. The company also delivers in-country support for its contractors.
VIEW WEBSITE
Key Facts
Initial investment: 10/08/2009
Sector – Business Services
Fund — Buyout Fund I
Status — Realised
Investment highlights
Increased global operational base through several new office openings including Japan, Russia, Iraq and Saudi Arabia.
Completed strategic acquisitions in Papua New Guinea and Singapore.
Sourced an independent non-executive director with vast experience across both the oil and gas industry and wider business services.
Worked with management to secure additional working capital facilities to support growth.
Doubled profitability in a three year period to circa £10.5m on exit.
Successfully exited the business in October 2012 via a secondary buyout, achieving a 3x return in just over three years.
Partnership Motivation

Strengthened the existing management team through the recruitment of a new finance director, marketing director and deputy medical director.
Successfully exited the business in 2022, with a revenue increase of 180% over the course of the investment.

We are excited by the opportunity to invest in a business with significant growth potential, through organic growth at existing sites and the rollout of new clinics across the UK, supported by the large, growing, but fragmented market. We are also impressed by management’s reputation in the market and Veincentre’s focus on quality of care which is attractive to consultants who work as part of the group.
“I am very proud of what the team has achieved over the last four years, helping more people get successful treatment for their varicose veins. Our strategy has been to grow our clinic base to make our services more accessible, whilst maintaining our high levels of clinical excellence and raising our profile through enhanced marketing campaigns. I am very grateful for the support offered by Palatine and the West family and look forward to our new partnership with CBPE and to continued success.”

The need The Hearing People addresses is one of the most pressing in the UK’s healthcare system. NHS waiting lists for audiology services have reached record levels, leaving millions of people waiting months, sometimes years, for assessments and treatment that could transform their quality of life. The Hearing People addresses that need directly, working in partnership with nine NHS Integrated Care Boards to deliver community-based hearing care that removes pressure from hospital services and gets patients seen faster, closer to home.
YFM backed the management buyout of The Hearing People in February 2025, bringing in experienced healthcare leadership alongside incumbent Managing Director Deep Patel, including Jon Lowe, former CEO of Connect Health, as non-executive chair. The combination of strong clinical expertise, deep NHS relationships and an experienced management team gives the business the foundations to expand significantly from its current footprint.
The macro case is straightforward: an ageing population, record NHS waiting times, and a government under sustained pressure to deliver community-based alternatives to hospital services. The Hearing People is operating in the right place, at the right time, with the right model.
“YFM are helping us to lay the foundations for the next phase of our growth journey. Their financial support is complemented by leading strategic insight, which will ensure we’re perfectly positioned to achieve our scale-up ambitions.”
Deep Patel, Managing Director at The Hearing People

The business supports customers ranging from individual sites to complex, multi-site operations, combining a substantial equipment fleet with nationwide engineering coverage and an expanding network of regional locations. Access Partnership
An international public policy ﬁrm that advises many of the world’s largest technology companies.
Investment highlights
The Business
Access is a fast-growing, international public policy ﬁrm that advises many of the world’s largest technology companies on matters ranging from data policy to infrastructure regulation and compliance.
Access is positioned at the heart of regulatory and technology change and has a deep understanding of both policy and technical aspects of dataﬂows and data delivery systems.
Headquartered in London, the business manages its international service offering from offices in the US, Africa, Asia and the Middle East. This operational scope enables Access to serve its world-leading multinational client base wherever their policy needs arise.
The Deal
Mobeus invested £13.1 million for a minority stake in the business, which has experienced rapid growth, with revenues doubling over the previous three years.
The Impact
With Mobeus’s backing Access and its team grew both organically and through acquisition. During the investment term, in addition to a £7 million refinancing, Mobeus helped Access to complete two bolt-on acquisitions in Singapore, adding c. £1.5 million to profits. This resulted in a doubling of the business in headcount to 120 people, and growth in revenues from £11 million to £25 million. 
The Realisation
Less than three years after the investment, Mobeus sold Access to Mayfair Equity Partners, a well regarded UK mid-market private equity firm. The sale delivered a 4.4x MoC and 64% IRR return for Mobeus 1.

Data capture technology for transportation and ticketing 
Investment highlights
The Business
Access’s innovative, miniaturised devices, such as passport and ticket readers, enable the world’s population to move around the planet and access services quickly, safely and securely; a challenge the current pandemic has made even more critical to resolve. Its engineers use advanced technologies in new ways, combining document imaging, barcode reading, NFC and RFID decoding, and contactless payments. As a result, Access is trusted by some of the world’s biggest brands, its hardware is present in more than 200 airports and over 100 million transactions are conducted daily through Access devices.
The Original Deal
We invested £11 million into Access-IS, investing alongside management for a significant minority stake. Our investment has been used to support the business’s further development into new verticals, such as ID and security, including providing solutions to global ATM suppliers, and to further expand its transport and ticketing solutions. In addition significant investment has gone into restructuring Access’s back office and infrastructure to ensure it’s able to deliver on its ambitious growth plans.
The Impact
Since Mobeus’s investment in 2015, Access delivered consistent year on year growth, nearly doubling revenue from £11.5m to over £19m in 2019. The business also professionalised its operations and substantially increased its production capacity.
The sale results in total cash proceeds for the Mobeus-advised VCTs of £27.8m, representing a 2.5x money multiple on original cost of £11.0m and an overall IRR of 23.4%.
The Realisation
In 2020, Mobeus realised its investment in Access in a sale to HID Corporation Ltd. a subsidiary of ASSA ABLOY, the global leader in access solutions, which owns the Chubb and Yale brands.

A leading European provider of financial protection insurance for the travel industry
Investment highlights
The Business
For 35 years, Assured Underwriting Group has specialised in financial protection insurance (surety bonds) for the travel industry. AUG operates as an MGA (Managing General Agent), vested with underwriting authority by its primary insurer partners.
The Deal
We invested in the management buyout of AUG in 2018. We led negotiations with the vendors and took time to understand this complex business, enabling us to complete the transaction just prior to the business’s peak trading period, which was a key requirement.  
The Impact
Mobeus supported AUG through a demanding period for the travel sector during Covid-19, then worked proactively with the management team to reposition the business towards international growth. With its skilled underwriting base and detailed understanding of the surety industry, AUG has expanded into 10 new markets in mainland Europe. We have supported the introduction of Carl Beardmore, a sector specialist Chairman, made three strategic bolt-ons and are targeting expansion of AUG’s travel offering into adjacent insurance areas. 
The Realisation
In June 2026, Mobeus agreed to sell AUG to ANV Group, a global insurance intermediary platform.  The sale is set to deliver in excess of a 4.0x MoC for Mobeus 1.

Investment highlights
Mobeus has substantially realised its investment in British International Holdings by way of a structured sale of its helicopter operations and its other assets.
British International Holdings held two major long-term contracts to provide helicopter support services to military operations in Plymouth and the Falkland Islands, and operated the scheduled passenger route between Penzance and the Isles of Scilly.
Original Deal
Funds advised by Mobeus backed the secondary MBO of the company from private equity investors in June 2006, investing £3.5 million.
Impact
The business began to face a structural decline, exacerbated by the recession, in the number of passengers flying to the Isles of Scilly. Mobeus actively assisted in the restructuring of the business, investing further funds to enable the group to close the unprofitable route and dispose of its principal property asset.
Further funds were also advanced to facilitate the sale of the company’s major military contracts, thereby preserving employment in the West Country and enabling an orderly winding down of activities.
Sale
In October 2012 the company’s property in Penzance was sold, followed in May 2013 by the sale to Patriot Aerospace of the company’s military contracts.
Mobeus Returns
The investment at cost of £4.7 million has generated total proceeds of £8.3 million (1.8x money).

As insurers, fleet operators and consumers increasingly prioritise convenience, speed and cost efficiency, Revive is well positioned to benefit from attractive long-term structural growth in the automotive aftercare market. With Mobeus’s support, the business will continue investing in its people, technology platform and commercial capability. Growth will be driven by expanding the franchise network, strengthening relationships with national accounts and entering adjacent market opportunities, building on Revive’s outstanding reputation for customer service.

The Business
At investment, Star Brands was primarily a supplier of own label cleaning and detergent products for UK retailers. Structural change in the grocery market enabled Star Brands to grow rapidly. However, the bigger opportunity was to reposition the business and build a challenger brand, The Pink Stuff, that took share from larger branded FMCG players.

Pink Stuff was repackaged and reformulated (with its now signature rhubarb fragrance). Star Brands used social media influencers to re-launch the brand which went viral, logging over 200 million monthly views and driving international growth – it is now sold in over 120 countries. The Pink Stuff was re-positioned outside the UK as a premium brand, and the range expanded to over 20 SKUs. In 2023 Mobeus led the acquisition of the US distributor which brought direct access to US retailers and almost doubled EBITDA. Over the investment, Star delivered growth of 5x in sales and 15x in EBITDA.
The Realisation
The business was acquired by RPM International Inc. for £345m (plus an earnout), a NYSE-listed company with global sales exceeding $7 billion and a diverse portfolio of market-leading brands such as Rust-Oleum, DAP, Carboline and Tremco.

Arthouse
Business Description
Arthouse is a leading designer and distributor of home decorative products and wall coverings to retail outlets both in the UK and overseas, across a range of sales channels and market sectors. NorthEdge invested in October 2015 and exited in December 2022.
Exit
Clare Bate, Managing Director of Arthouse, said: “Since investment, we have been focussed on building a sustainable business, investing in our people, product and e-commerce capabilities.
“However, recent macro-economic challenges have seen our operating costs increase materially, alongside a rapid decline in consumer demand. As a result, over the last two years, we have been working closely with our shareholders, banking partners and specialist advisors to stabilise the business through the tough trading conditions, safeguarding the future of the Arthouse brand and its talented team.
“This acquisition provides Arthouse with an opportunity to continue creating inspirational products and serving our valued customers, I would like to thank everyone across the business and all key stakeholders for their ongoing support and I look forward to becoming part of the Esselle group.”

Bridge Farm Group
Background
Bridge Farm Group is one of the UK’s leading growers of ornamental plants, flowers and herbs. Founded in 1988, the company operates from five locations around Spalding, Lincolnshire, including its flagship 75-acre site.
The company sells more than 80 million plants and flowers per year to retailers and consumers across the globe, including major UK supermarkets. Bridge Farm Group has a workforce of over 500 employees.
NorthEdge Exit
NorthEdge supported the MBO of Bridge Farm in August 2017. The investment, from Fund II, enabled the company to deliver a capital expenditure programme and develop its highly differentiated market proposition.
This included the construction of a new £18m production facility, which was part funded by a further £5m investment from NorthEdge, in May 2018. Located in Clay Lake, Spalding, the facility is a significant upgrade on the group’s previous 10-acre production facility at Horseshoe Road, featuring biomass heating alongside a range of automated handling systems to improve efficiency.
Since NorthEdge’s investment, Bridge Farm has increased sales from £12m to £15.4m, achieving gross profit of £3.8m.
NorthEdge announced its exit in July 2019, in a trade sale to Canadian firm, Sundial Growers Inc.

Business Description
Contollo Group (Contollo) is a newly formed built environment consultancy group that supports clients across a range of sectors to achieve their regulatory and sustainability targets in the built environment.
Background
Our investment will allow Contollo to undertake a UK-focused buy and build strategy, which will support the business to serve the rapidly increasing demand for tech-enabled smart buildings. This demand is driven by board-level ESG agendas and underpinned by growing regulatory pressure on built environment stakeholders to progress towards Net Zero.
Our investment backs Oliver Dennis, Executive Chair, and Ruth Percival, CEO, who both bring significant M&A and Private Equity experience in the professional services sector to build the platform. 
The deal was funded from NorthEdge SME Fund I and led by Ray Stenton, Managing Partner; Liam May, Director; Matthew Mellon, Investment Manager; and Sam Allen, Investment Manager. 
Liam May will join the board on behalf of NorthEdge.

Cubic Motion
Business Description
Cubic Motion is an award-winning facial animation studio and developer of advanced computer vision technologies.
Background
Headquartered at Manchester Science Park, Cubic Motion specialises in producing performance vision technology for real-time applications in social virtual reality, computer games and film production.
The business has created advanced digital content for a range of prominent video game publishers including Activision, Epic, EA, Ninja Theory and Sony, and has worked on prominent video game titles such as Call of Duty and Hellblade.
Cubic Motion employs over 70 internationally acclaimed computer vision researchers, engineers, animators and producers to create high quality solutions for a range of domestic and international clients.
NorthEdge Exit
In March 2020, NorthEdge completed the sale of Cubic Motion to Epic Games, which marks its second exit from Fund II.
NorthEdge’s investment in September 2017 unlocked the next phase of growth for Cubic Motion, which saw the business expand into US markets with a permanent presence in Los Angeles and transition into new headquarters at Manchester Science Park.

Business Description
Cysiam is a founder-led cyber security consultancy and managed services provider. The business provides advanced technical cyber consultancy solutions to the most secure aspects of governments globally, alongside a managed service offering to public and private sector customers within the UK – typically with clients with global supply chain exposure or critical infrastructure dependencies.
Background
Cyber Security services has been a sub-sector focus area for NorthEdge since 2021. In 2026, the UK cyber security services market is sized at £5.3bn and is experiencing growth in excess of 10% per annum.
Cysiam is globally recognised for deploying ex-government and military experts to build cyber resilience capabilities, as well as supporting complex international development and national infrastructure security projects. This has enabled the business to achieve rapid growth over three years prior to our investment.
The investment was funded from NorthEdge Fund IV and was led by Jon Pickering, Dan Matkin, Aiden Hawkes and Andy Royle.

Direct Healthcare Group
Business Description
Direct Healthcare Group (DHG) is a fully integrated developer and manufacturer of a range of innovative pressure care products designed to prevent medical issues such as pressure sores, which can lead to serious, sometimes life threatening diseases.
Background
Founded in 2009, the business works with care providers in over 20 countries throughout Europe and internationally. As a recognised world leader in the development of pressure care technologies, DHG is a winner of the prestigious Queen’s Award for Enterprise in Innovation.
NorthEdge Exit
NorthEdge completed the sale of DHG in a secondary buyout by European healthcare specialist investor ArchiMed.
The deal sees NorthEdge secure a 3x return on its initial investment, with an IRR of 39 per cent. NorthEdge led a management buyout of Direct Healthcare Services in April 2016, renamed it Direct Healthcare Group and broadened the firm’s product range through a series of bolt-on acquisitions.

DW3
Background
DW3 Products Group is a UK provider of high-quality, premium door solutions and window systems. 
NorthEdge originally invested in Solidor in October 2014 after recognising the enormous potential of the manufacturing sector. Led by Solidor CEO Gareth Mobley, DW3 Products Group was formed in November 2014 to create a platform to buy and build innovative manufacturers. The business made two further follow-on acquisitions, and now supplies products under brand names Solidor, Residor, Nicedor, and Residence.
Solidor utilises a leading online offering, including a door designer and a specialised online portal, which allows trade customers to specify and purchase products online.
NorthEdge Exit
NorthEdge completed the sale of DW3 to Masonite International Corporation, the NYSE-listed global designer and manufacturer of interior and exterior doors, in January 2018.
The transaction is NorthEdge’s eighth exit from Fund I and represents a 3.5x return and an IRR of 59 per cent with a holding period of 40 months.

Help-Link
Background
Headquartered in Leeds, Help-Link is a UK market leader in energy efficient domestic boiler and central heating installation, service and maintenance.
Founded in 1998, the company has enjoyed considerable growth over recent years and has invested heavily in its delivery capability and operational platform. This enabled the company to offer exceptional customer service using the highest quality products on the market at an affordable price.
NorthEdge backed the company in April 2013 and was attracted to Help-Link because of its strong market position and reputation for excellent customer service. Help-Link had invested heavily in its operational platform, systems and infrastructure to create a business of scale with a strong national footprint.
NorthEdge Exit
Following NorthEdge’s investment, Help-Link went on to further strengthen its senior management team with key appointments during 2015/16 and secured significant national relationships with blue chip companies such as EDF Energy as a result.
NorthEdge announced its exit of Help-Link in August 2017. The company entered into an agreement to be acquired by international home repairs and improvements group HomeServe plc, in a move that marked the next step in the company’s growth and allowed HomeServe to create a new UK-wide home heating business – bringing together installations, servicing and repairs. The deal valued the Help-Link business at up to £22.7m.

Background
Decision intelligence, an emerging discipline, bridges the gap between data analytics and real-world decision making. Hublsoft wraps a human-centric user experience around this concept, making it universally understandable and accessible.
Strategy
The merger enhances the Hublsoft core technology platform, integrating automation capabilities into their decision intelligence suite. By integrating the iPortalis technology, automation can be applied to a number of decision scenarios; particularly where significant operational and cost efficiencies can be achieved, such as the automated optimisation of cloud or software licensing economics. This is critical for businesses, providing immediate cost-saving solutions whilst protecting capacity and business performance.

Business Description
Oak Engage provides a mobile-first employee engagement and intranet platform which supports businesses to build a strong culture, enhance productivity and boost operational efficiency.
Background
Headquartered in Newcastle, Oak Engage is trusted by major brands such as NatWest Group, ScS, Burger King UK, Five Guys, Aldi, and Halfords and has achieved strong growth with clients that are seeking to engage a disparate, frontline worker employee base. 
The customisable platform acts as a central hub to reach and engage deskless workforces, giving them easy access to company news and key documents. It also uses AI to deliver personalised communications, making it as easy as possible to get the right message, to the right people, at the right time – wherever they are located.
The company’s success has been driven by a senior leadership team who have extensive experience in scaling software businesses. Jake Armstrong, CFO, joined the business in 2021 following an expansive career in practice and industry, including acting as a fractional CFO for a number of Tech and SaaS organisations.

Ramsdens Financial Limited is a diversified, financial services provider and retailer with branches across North East England, Yorkshire, Scotland and Wales.
Founded in 1987 in Stockton-on-Tees, Ramsdens is a recognised and respected high street retailer of financial services, serving over 700,000 customers nationwide. The business operates in the four core business segments of foreign currency exchange, pawnbroking loans, the buying and selling of precious metals and the retailing of second hand and new jewellery.
NorthEdge Exit
NorthEdge initially backed the business in a management buyout in September 2014. The firm successfully floated the company on the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) of the London Stock Exchange in February 2017. The IPO represented a partial exit for NorthEdge, with the firm retaining a significant minority stake until December 2017, when the residual stake was sold generating strong returns.
Since the initial investment, NorthEdge supported the management team to consolidate the store estate, grow Ramsdens’ foreign exchange services and invest in the retail jewellery offering. This resulted in a more diversified business and a robust platform for future growth. Our investment will see Torbay strengthen its capabilities and significantly expand its reach in North America, while continuing to grow and invest in its 250-strong team at its UK headquarters in Paignton, Devon.                         Blaze Signs                    
Blaze Signs are market leaders in business signage and offers national retailers the complete signage solution, from project management and design through to manufacture and installation. Having won the prestigious Sign Company of the Year (30+ employees) award at the Sign & Wrap Awards 2024, Blaze Signs is eminently qualified to handle the logistical planning and project management, design, manufacture, and installation of any project, for any client, large or small.
We continually invest in training and development, along with investment to our production facilities in both Broadstairs and Birmingham to ensure we can provide a superior signage solution. Our designers breathe life into our clients’ brands with inspirational concepts, producing stunning visuals in 2D and 3D. Ideas move effortlessly from screen to reality within one of the largest signage manufacturing facilities in Europe, which is then installed by a team of certified engineers who are widely considered the gold standard in the industry.
Blaze Signs are 100% committed to sustainability and use the latest technology in their methods of manufacture to reduce emissions, waste material and energy use. Alongside sustainable materials, Blaze’s signage solutions are designed to decrease energy use, ensure longevity, and to minimise environmental impacts from their products and components during their entire lifecycle.
Blaze Signs work across a variety of different sectors and industries, including retail, hospitality, financial, EV charging and more. Some of the UK’s largest brands including Sainsbury’s, Motor Fuel Group, Tesco, IMO Car Wash, Next, and Waitrose trust Blaze Signs with their signage requirements.

                        Cygnia Maintenance                    
Cygnia Maintenance is the UK’s largest and leading provider of sign maintenance, sign repairs and image protection services. With a national network of sign maintenance engineers, 24/7 help desk support and a commitment to delivering the highest levels of customer service, customers can feel assured that Cygnia Maintenance is the right company to manage their sign maintenance requirements. Cygnia Maintenance offers both a reactive service and also a planned preventive maintenance service, so all customer maintenance needs are covered.
Along with their comprehensive signage maintenance services that cover all bases, Cygnia Maintenance also provide signage audit services, which provide their customers with a level of detail that makes estate decision-making easier than ever.
Every business has a duty of care to their staff and customers – maintaining safe signage is essential to deliver this duty. Cygnia Maintenance’s aim is to provide a cost-effective sign maintenance service in order to achieve optimal levels of sign safety across their customers’ entire estates. Their flexible reactive support services allow customers to meet the challenging and changing needs of their estate, and their 24/7/365 help desk provides a single point of contact for management of all reactive sign maintenance and image protection services.
A number of the largest brands in the UK place their trust in Cygnia Maintenance with their signage maintenance requirements, whether that’s planned preventative or reactive, including; ODEON, Caffe Nero, Sainsbury’s, Ladbrokes, Tesco and many others.

Collectia
Founded in 1998 and based in Brøndby, Denmark, Collectia is a fast-growing debt collection and debt purchase business operating primarily in Denmark with a niche presence in Sweden, Norway and Germany. The company employs more than 175 staff and serves about 13,000 corporate customers across more than 600,000 active cases.
Collectia is a highly differentiated business with a sophisticated proprietary technology platform, credit database and advanced data analytics capabilities. It has significant potential to build market share in existing and new markets.
The company has diversified beyond its core debt collection business in recent years. It has increased its exposure to debt purchasing and launched a credit control service for the Danish market, where Collectia provides credit score information to its customers. In addition, Collectia has carried out several acquisitions to expand its presence across the Nordic region and in Germany.
Our investment
The investment in Collectia builds on our extensive experience in the financial services sector and complements our strategy of leveraging attractive macro dynamics - in this case, increasing regulation and technology change.
New Danish and European Union-wide regulation is driving continued outsourcing of debt collection to specialist service providers such as Collectia. Furthermore, Collectia expects additional regulation will result in banks and businesses selling greater volumes of non-performing loans or debtor portfolios in the coming years.
Our investment will enable Collectia to accelerate its growth by using superior technology to develop its debt collection processes, scale its debt purchase operations, and continue its international expansion through selective acquisitions.

Sigma Components
Sigma is a leading component supplier serving the global commercial aerospace sector.
Based in the UK, it is a precision engineering manufacturer specialising in aerospace pipes, ducts, fabrications and precision surface finishing. Its customers include engineering company Rolls Royce, aerospace company Safran, aircraft manufacturer Airbus, planes and trains manufacturer Bombardier and defence and aerospace company BAE Systems.
At the time of our investment, in 2016, it had 3 manufacturing locations in the UK and two in China and employed about 750 people. It has a team of more than 40 engineers and a strong record of bringing new products to market.
Our investment
We identified Sigma as a strong investment opportunity due to it supplying mission critical components on growing aircraft programmes and due to significant potential to grow its manufacturing operations in China.
Silverfleet’s previous experience of supporting international expansion, including in China, made us the ideal partner for Sigma. We have enhanced its production capacity in China to complement Sigma’s UK operations in order to provide leading, high quality component manufacturing for customers and to help them by demonstrating “local content” when they supply engines / aircraft to Chinese airlines.
Part of our attraction to the deal was also the opportunity for Sigma to buy Rolls Royce’s internal pipe manufacturing facility in the UK, which would greatly benefit from Sigma’s leading manufacturing management processes and international capacity. This acquisition was integral to Sigma’s growth.
Value creation
Much of our value creation plan for Sigma is based on fundamental operational improvement. We have increased the capacity of the Xi’an and Chengdu sites in China to satisfy demand and capitalise on the high quality of the products made by Sigma’s China teams.
Previously, Sigma’s teams in China would make a limited number of components, which would then arrive at the company’s UK sites to be assembled and finished before being shipped to customers. We have increased the number of components that Sigma’s sites in China are approved to make from 20 to 450 following substantial investment in staff, machinery and training. Why Synectics Solutions?
Synectics was founded in 1992 to leverage software and data to help organisations identify and prevent financial crime. Over three decades, the Company built a unique syndicated fraud database operating on a “give-to-get” model, where customers share fraud data in exchange for access to the collective dataset. Today, the platform contains over 300 million records, processed through a proprietary analytics engine to detect and prevent fraud across financial services, utilities and government
Strategy
Post investment, Synectics is harnessing data in two principal ways: to enable scalable growth through operational improvement and to enhance value creation within its product offering.
First, Synectics has embedded a data-centric operating model to improve pace, coordination and execution discipline. Historically, data sat across fragmented systems, limiting visibility and slowing decision making. Since investment, the rollout of a new ERP backbone, contract management platform, CRM infrastructure and workflow tools has created a more integrated data layer across the business. This provides real-time performance visibility, clearer pipeline oversight and tighter execution tracking. The aim is to improve operational rhythm, accelerate data-driven decisions and support growth without a corresponding increase in organisational complexity.

The Company has built a comprehensive suite of software solutions spanning parking enforcement, permitting and traffic management, with strong positions in both private parking and the Local Authority market. Structural drivers, including digitisation of enforcement, adoption of ANPR technology and increasing outsourcing within local government, provided clear long-term growth tailwinds. At investment, Unity5 had a strong product set and customer base, but required leadership depth and enhanced go-to-market capability to unlock its full potential.
Strategy
The first priority was professionalising and strengthening the leadership team. The Synova Talent team supported the hire of the Chairman, then helped deliver a structured founder succession plan, including the hiring of a Chief Commercial Officer who was subsequently transitioned into the Chief Executive Officer role and an HR Director to replace the founders. 
Senior capability was further enhanced through targeted hires across finance (including a Chief Finance Officer), marketing, go-to-market and operations (including a Chief Operating Officer). The Synova Talent team also worked alongside management to scope and support the hire of a new Chief Product & Technology Officer to lead long-term product and platform development.

Expana had a strong customer base in the UK when we invested but with a limited presence in Europe and in the US and with investment required across the business to help them scale we had to really lean in to deliver growth. Our expertise in data and tech – coupled with our experience growing B2B data and software businesses – meant we were well-placed to help Expana scale up. It was clear that we shared management’s vision for the Company, and we're in agreement about how to reach those goals. Shortly thereafter, we got to work.
Strategy
Modernisation started with a move from enterprise software to the cloud. We built advanced analytics into the platform, providing key insights for the newly-headed marketing team. Crucially, we entered new markets in order to expand the dataset and provide additional value to customers.
Prior to our investment, there was no dedicated sales and marketing function at Expana. So we helped the team to build sales teams in Europe and the US, with dedicated marketing functions to drive new leads. Together with a structured approach to account management we managed to quadruple ARR during the first phase of our ownership.
Further increasing the already high ROI and value proposition of Expana to its customers was a key lever to driving value and growth. We supported them to invest in a proprietary data team, achieving IOSCO-accreditation and making them the first food-focused PRA in the world. We also identified, negotiated and executed the acquisition of Danish commodities forecasting specialist, Kairos, fully rounding out the price insight capabilities of the Expana platorm.

At the time of investment, adopting automation in IT operations was a structural tailwind, rather than cyclical demand. Enterprise IT environments were becoming increasingly complex, hybridised and distributed, driving a clear need for automation-led operations and predictive remediation. We believed AIOps represented a durable and expanding category, with automation shifting from a productivity enhancement to an operational necessity. Within that context, Avantra was well positioned at the intersection of SAP specialisation and intelligent automation, offering both defensible niche focus and broader category upside.

As part of our partnership, we supported a founder transition, bringing in Ashley Read (formerly CMO of Science in Sport plc) to lead the brand through the next phase. Since then, Sneak has expanded into RTD cans across various flavour combinations, growing to 14,000 UK distribution points (and growing fast).

About
Soulfresh was founded in 2003 with one van in Melbourne, Australia, with the aim of changing the way people eat and drink for the better. The business takes a stand against unimaginative brands dominating supermarkets, with a sustainable and uncompromising approach to food.
Soulfresh operates its own brands across three core categories - fermented (living) beverages, plant-based products, and drinks - including Emma & Tom's, Lo Bros (organic kombucha) and Not Soda. It also distributes a range of third-party brands, serving an international footprint spanning Australia, New Zealand, the UK, and beyond.
Our journey with Soulfresh:
We invested at the end of 2019. We believe in the mission to disrupt food and beverage with healthier, more sustainable alternatives, and think the time is right for progressive businesses to reimagine the industry. We brought in Ben Clarke - former CEO of Burton's Biscuit Company and former chair of Grenade - as independent chairman.
In 2024, Soulfresh acquired Emma & Tom's, a well-loved Australian brand and certified B Corp known for its commitment to health and wellness. Founded on the principle of "looking after yourself," Emma & Tom's has been a family favourite for nearly 20 years, offering a diverse range of nutritious juices, smoothies and snacks made from the highest quality, mostly Australian ingredients. Post-acquisition, we've taken the brand internationally to New Zealand.

Ambassador Theatre Group

Exponent formed ATG through the concurrent acquisition and merger of Ambassador Theatres, the second-largest theatre group in the UK, and LiveNation’s UK theatres. In these efforts, we worked closely with Chairperson Greg Dyke, former Director General of the BBC and Chair of the FA and BFI, alongside ATG’s founders and co-CEOs Sir Howard Panter and Rosemary Squire.
Not only does ATG benefit from strong long-term growth driven by the live entertainment trend, its distinctive vertically-integrated model - with operations spanning venue management, ticketing and production - ensures ATG is well-positioned to lead innovation within the industry.
In November 2013, Providence Equity Partners

, with Exponent retaining a minority interest in the business. We sold the remainder of our interest to Providence in November 2016.

We were attracted to Fintrax Group as it is the technology leader in the VAT refund market and is very well positioned to benefit from continued growth in tourism, especially from emerging economies. Exponent acquired Fintrax Group in 2012 from the entrepreneur who had founded the business in the 1980s. We acquired the business with John Moore as buy-in Chairperson. Exponent acquired V.Group, alongside management, in March 2007, appointing David Hoare as Chairperson and Clive Richardson as CEO to help focus and professionalise the business. Under our ownership, the business made three acquisitions: RCC in Norway, ITM in Dubai and MUM in Singapore.
We were attracted to the business by its long-term growth prospects which were underpinned by the robust growth in world trade and the global shipping fleet, and the trend towards outsourcing to third party ship managers. This was being driven by the increasing regulatory burden, a growth in financial owners and a shortage of trained labour. V.Group’s scale, reputation and technical leadership afforded it significant competitive advantages and also made it well-placed to lead the consolidation of a fragmented industry.
In September 2011, Exponent 
completed the sale
 of V.Group to OMERS Private Equity for $520m.

Vibrant Foods

The business produces a range of pulses, spices, flours and other Indian food ingredients which are sold under the Vibrant Food brand primarily through independent South Asian stores as well as the supermarket channel. The group is made up of the TRS, East End Foods, Cofresh, Everest Dairies and Fudco brands.
The company was formed by Exponent through the acquisition of TRS and East End Foods, which had been owned by their founding families (the Suterwallas and Wouhras, respectively) since the 1960s.
We were attracted to TRS & East End Foods due to their strong brand and loyal consumer following, and the favourable growth dynamics in ethnic foods consumption across the UK and continental Europe. The Opportunity
Anochrome is one of Europe’s leading providers of specialist surface coatings, corrosion protection and thread-locking sealant systems for performance critical products in demanding environments. The effect was to drive a focus on sales, margins, the achievement of synergies such that the group significantly outperformed its peer group.
By 2020, we had acquired 60 businesses, and had become a leading independent insurance broker in the UK. The scale, stability and growth in profitability led to a very strong partial exit, with Penta delivering 3.3x money for our investors.
Following the 2020 transaction Penta maintained a minority equity interest as the GRP group continued to grow to become one of the top three independent brokers in the UK with GWP under influence of £1.8bn.
In 2022 GRP was sold to Brown & Brown, a US publicly traded insurance broker, which delivered a further significant return to investors.

The Business
The Advantage Healthcare Rutland deal brought together a number of nationally known BUPA-owned businesses, namely BUPA Nursing, Strand Nurses, Montpellier Health Care and Professional Healthcare Services. The businesses provide temporary doctors, nurses, specialist nurses, allied health professionals and carers enabling NHS and private care providers to cover staff shortfalls and fluctuating workloads. Advantage Healthcare had a network of 25 branches with a database of over 6,500 workers and a number of preferred supplier arrangements, including the NHS and BUPA itself.
Investment thesis
On acquisition, the business was a non-core business of BUPA operating in a market with significant challenges due to the structural changes impacting the NHS staffing market and healthcare sector. Post carve-out, the strategy was to transition the business activities from the declining healthcare staffing market to the higher growth home healthcare provision market. To facilitate this strategy, investment was made in appropriate central resources to enable managed growth into home healthcare provision. Centralisation of worker recruitment, training and compliance were key areas of focus and the website was also developed into a key tool for recruiting workers and promoting the business.
Exit
By exit, Advantage Healthcare was a leading UK provider of home healthcare and healthcare staffing services with a network of 27 branches and a large database of healthcare workers. The business worked with Primary Care Trusts (PCTs), insurers and private individuals to provide high quality care for people in their homes. Home healthcare represented c.10% of revenues at acquisition and by exit this proportion had risen to c.80%. The business was successfully sold to a Trade buyer, Interserve, delivering a 2.6x money multiple for investors.

The Business
The AFI Group is a leading specialist equipment hire business that provides mobile elevating work platforms as well as complementary specialist skills and compliance training and resale operations. The Group comprises of a comprehensive network of branches both in the UK and Middle East (Bahrain, UAE, Qatar and Saudi Arabia). Customers in the UK are predominantly in the repair and maintenance sector with Middle East operations construction and infrastructure focused.
Investment thesis
The initial transaction was a simultaneous merger of three businesses, AFI-Uplift and Hi-Reach in the UK (3,700 and 1,500 machines respectively) and ARG (400 machines) in the Middle East. The transaction enabled AFI to cement its position as a leading operator in the powered access rental market and create an enlarged group that was well placed for further growth. This common ownership also created fleet utilisation opportunities with the movement of surplus UK assets across to the higher growth Middle East market. Further acquisitions were a core part of the investment thesis, increasing the number of machines in the group’s rental fleet as well as further developing the group’s geographic and end market focus, product and service offering and driving better fleet utilisation. The growth plans also involved expansion in the Middle East; specifically the roll out of depots in Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Bahrain. A final key aspect of the investment plan was to invest in AFI’s own in-house transport fleet to control the delivery process ensuring quick delivery and collection of the rental fleet.
Exit
AFI grew strongly during Rutland’s investment period, with numerous bolt-on acquisitions, new depots in both the UK and Middle East, a broadening of its service offering and more than doubling its fleet of powered access machines.  This resulted in AFI’s revenue increasing from c.£50m at acquisition to over £100m at its exit to Pricoa Private Capital in a £160m transaction.

The Business
Attends is the trading name of the European operations formerly known as PaperPak. Attends manufactures and supplies a wide range of branded and own label healthcare products used to assist both users and carers dealing with incontinence. In general, the products have historically been reimbursed to the ultimate user and sold through a variety of channels to institutions, health funds and providers across all principal markets in Northern and Western Europe. There is also a growing trend of cash sales at retail. The business is based in the UK but its principal manufacturing operations are located in Aneby, Sweden.
Investment thesis
Attends Healthcare needed a hands-on investor with the courage and commitment to tackle multiple challenges simultaneously. Operational re-structuring was needed to lower costs, upgrade the product portfolio, win new customers and create a modern and highly efficient production facility. The focus was on transitioning the Attends product portfolio which was focused on incontinence products to the dynamic and fast-growing market of primarily female buyers for light to moderate pads and pull-ons. To facilitate this strategic product shift, a capex investment plan was devised to build a new high-speed production line. In the nearer term, the plan was based on a number of further operational improvements including warehouse system upgrades, line rationalisation projects, initiatives to speed up lines, and supply chain management improvements.
Exit
In January 2012 Attends was sold to Trade, Canadian Domtar Corporation, delivering a 3.3x money multiple for investors. The Trade player already owned the Attends US business and planned to align this to the European divisions post-acquisition.

The Business
Brandon Hire is a leading tool and equipment hire business with headquarters in Bristol which operated a national network of over 140 depots. The business services a wide range of customers with c.30,000 local trade and smaller business accounts as well as national contracts with larger customers. Customers principally operate in a range of maintenance, building and service sectors. The business had approximately 900 employees across the group. Brandon was previously part of Wolseley Plc and the original transaction was a complex carve-out taking eighteen months to complete with a number of sites shared with its former parent.
Investment thesis
The initial focus of the plan was to implement a successful, clean separation from Wolseley, exiting shared sites whilst retaining the bulk of the revenues and key clients, establishing an independent, standalone business under a refocused brand. Post separation, the core strategy was to further develop the company as the leading national player focused on the local market, capitalising on the attractive growth opportunity in local repair and maintenance as well as maximising asset efficiency and utilisation together with implementing a number of other projects and margin initiatives. Selective M&A also formed part of the investment thesis strengthening and broadening Brandon’s offering with further investment in the team additionally planned.
Exit
The successful implementation of the Group’s strategy following the complex carve-out from Wolseley, enabled Brandon Hire to achieve strong earnings growth with development of the business through site, product and service expansion supported by investment in the team and systems together with M&A. A strong reputation in the marketplace as a well-run, well-positioned business, which remained highly invested, made Brandon Hire attractive strategically to a wide range of buyers and Rutland successfully completed the sale of Brandon Hire to Vp plc, a UK listed specialist rental group, delivering a 2.6x money multiple to investors.

The Business
Buy As You View is a retail and consumer finance business selling a range of electrical and household goods on three-year hire purchase agreements. Customers have limited access to credit and make low regular weekly payments without the requirement of an upfront deposit or conventional credit check. Payment discipline is managed through a meter and customers are serviced through a field-based sales and collection workforce. The business was acquired from a syndicate of banks who had taken control from a financial sponsor.
Investment thesis
The initial equity investment in BAYV was underpinned by a solvent run-off of the loan book. The investment plan was centered on developing and better utilising technology across the business including both collections and sales. Firstly, stability and control of the business was achieved, followed by development of a “smart meter” to improve the control and performance of the loan book. The plan then revolved around restoring the business to controlled, self-funded growth.
Exit
The initial deal was done all equity, with a major refinancing achieved in 2014. In 2015, the business was caught up in a wider review of the rent-to-own sector by the FCA which severely restricted the ability of the sector to write new loans and resulting in a restructuring deal done with the lending banks.
